cases.prompt: Audit files/sloppy-announcement.md for AI writing patterns. Don't rewrite it, I just want to see what's wrong.
expected_behavior: Quotes at least three offending phrases or lines verbatim from the file, such as "Here's the thing" or "Experts agree"
Names the pattern for each quoted item and gives a fix in a few words
Does not provide a rewritten version of the paragraphs
Does not claim or guess that an AI wrote the text

cases.prompt: Edit files/release-draft.md to remove the AI-sounding parts. Return the edited text.
expected_behavior: Output contains none of the banned words leverage, robust, streamline, delve, or the phrases "This is huge" and "Let that sink in"
Keeps the concrete facts: the Tuesday cut, the 40-minute regression suite, and Mina Okafor
Does not rewrite the plain first paragraph beyond minimal fixes

check.cmd: ! grep -qiE '—|leverage|robust|streamline|delve|this is huge|let that sink in' output.txt

cases.prompt: I'm about to commit files/cache_sync.py with the message in files/commit-message.txt. Run stop-slop over both and tell me what to change before I commit.
expected_behavior: Flags T-17 and IG-6 in the code comment of cache_sync.py for removal and says to describe what the retry does instead
Flags the internal nickname "Bluebird" or the AC-3 reference in the code comment
Leaves commit-message.txt alone on the ticket IDs, stating that commit messages are the acceptable place for them
Notes the multi-line comment block above fetch_with_retry exceeds 1-2 lines and should be trimmed

cases.prompt: Write a short explanation of the change in files/change-notes.md for a teammate who has never seen this service. They are reviewing it tomorrow.
expected_behavior: Has distinct what, why, and evidence parts, with the why naming the rejected alternative of failing the whole export
Evidence separates what local tests proved from what is not yet proved on staging or in CI
States plainly that no live PR or CI run exists yet and does not imply the nightly job was verified
Uses the concrete failure (invoices with a null due_date silently dropped) rather than words like improved reliability

cases.prompt: This blog intro reads like ChatGPT wrote it. Tighten it and strip the AI tells: "In today's fast-paced world, it's worth noting that teams must leverage robust tooling to navigate the ever-evolving landscape."
Explain my invoice export fix to a reviewer who doesn't know the repo: what changed, why, and what the tests prove versus what a live CI run would prove.
Tighten the onboarding overview page in docs/ so it is summary-first with progressive disclosure and links to the detail pages.
